doc.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011

title: Why he left Lou Rawls, and duties as musical director
summary: Rawls's disco turn, year-round work, screening unsolicited song tapes, and TV appearances like The Tonight Show.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh I didn’t know it went that far. Do you recall why you left Lou Rawls to try those other people?

Well the situation was we had some personnel changes. The type of stuff that we were doing, I wasn’t that crazy about. Lou was kind of learning towards more of a disco thing and it got away from — I didn’t like the songs as much. By that time — now on Lou’s gig it was 52 weeks a year even if the other guys had a few days off here or there, being the musical director I did not, so a lot of times I would have to go with the boss to his home in LA and, for example, if he was going to do a recording date he would get a lot of unsolicited material and so part of my gig was to go through the boxes of tapes and little acetate records and cassettes and stuff, to try to find material that the publishing company would say well we’ve got some stuff here but if you’ve got something of your own, well great. And this is something else for aspiring songwriters, the people that check out your stuff to see if they want to record it? They listen to about ten seconds. Because you’re checking out — if there’s a long introduction you fast forward it because you can’t be wasting your time, and you can pretty much tell right away if this is something you think you’re going to listen to. So if the good stuff is in the middle of the song it never gets heard. So, but anyway, between all of that stuff if there was a TV show very often, like “The Tonight Show,” when we did that, and I did that a bunch of times, I would go. The whole band wouldn’t go. They would use their rhythm section. So again, guys were off, I’m over there working still. So by the end of this time I wanted to come home, I wanted to start a family, I didn’t have a child at that time, and so I made a decision that the road is not what I want to do. It’s not what I thought it was going to be. Let me go home.
